 13|
 14|# Product Owner Flow Templates
 15|
 16|Copy/apply patterns for Product Owner Flow Mode models.
 17|
 18|**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, with `references/flow-mode.md` whenever Flow intent is selected
 19|**Purpose:** Provides the user-flow patterns, the provenance table every diagram type keeps and the reply shape every type delivers
 20|**Scope:** Five user-flow patterns, the intake questions, the provenance table and the reply shape. The other types keep their patterns in `assets/templates/`
 21|**Output Path:** None. The model is working data and the board is the deliverable
 22|
 23|---
 24|
 25|## 1. OVERVIEW
 26|
 27|### Purpose
 28|
 29|Every pattern below passes `scripts/flow_check.py` as a user flow, and `scripts/compose_board.py` composes it into a board. Start from the pattern closest to the flow, rename the nodes after the real screens and triggers, add the board lines below and run the check before the write gate. A process, an architecture, a sequence, a state diagram, an ER diagram or a gantt chart starts from its own file in `assets/templates/`, and keeps the provenance table and the reply shape below.
 30|
 31|### Usage
 32|
 33|- Node ids are short, stable and camelCase, because the provenance table names them, the composer names every layer after them and the generated fallback mis-routes an underscore
 34|- A label names the screen or the action a person takes, in the words the product uses, in one to four words where those words allow
 35|- A label with a parenthesis, a colon or a slash goes in double quotes, such as `pick["Pick a plan (monthly)"]`
 36|- A decision label is a question, and each exit label is one of its answers
 37|- Every connector is a solid arrow `-->`
 38|- A user flow and a process each carry exactly one `style` line, which marks the first glance. A styled goal, failing end or decision keeps its kind and takes a pink outline, and a styled step is drawn light pink. `style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575` makes that end the goal and the light red pair makes an end a failure. Every pair comes from `references/style-guide.md`, and any other colour is refused or counts as a second accent
 39|- Write `flowchart LR` unless the chain is short, because a board reads wider than it reads tall
 40|
 41|### Board lines
 42|
 43|The board's own text rides on `%%` comment lines, which the check ignores and the composer reads. Each one is optional, and the generated fallback strips them all:
 44|
 45|```text
 46|%% title: Start a return
 47|%% subtitle: How a customer starts a return in the app, from the order list to a confirmed return
 48|%% source: Sources: five app screenshots and the returns doc. Left out: free pickup over 100 euros, a proposal.
 49|%% zone: Find the order: orders, detail
 50|%% zone: Request the return: window, reason, method
 51|```
 52|
 53|- `%% title:` names the board. With none, the composer takes a Mermaid frontmatter title, a sequence or gantt `title` line, then `Diagram <n>`
 54|- `%% subtitle:` is one sentence under the title on who reads the board and why
 55|- `%% source:` is the line under the key naming the sources and what was left out
 56|- `%% zone: <label>: <id>, <id>` groups nodes in a tinted section. A user flow or a process without lanes reads its zones in flow order, and once a flow has zones every node sits in exactly one. An ER diagram draws each zone around its entities. Lanes and composite states are zones already, so a laned process, an architecture or a state diagram takes no zone line
 57|
 58|---
 59|
 60|## 2. PATTERNS
 61|
 62|### Linear flow
 63|
 64|```mermaid
 65|flowchart TD
 66|    start([Open the page]) --> step1[Fill in the form]
 67|    step1 --> step2[Submit]
 68|    step2 --> done([Confirmation shown])
 69|    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
 70|```
 71|
 72|### One decision
 73|
 74|```mermaid
 75|flowchart TD
 76|    start([Open the page]) --> step1[Submit the form]
 77|    step1 --> valid{Valid?}
 78|    valid -->|Yes| done([Confirmation shown])
 79|    valid -->|No| fix[Show the field errors]
 80|    fix --> step1
 81|    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
 82|```
 83|
 84|### Platform split with a merge dot
 85|
 86|```mermaid
 87|flowchart TD
 88|    start([Open the page]) --> open[Open the selector]
 89|    open --> device{Which device?}
 90|    device -->|Desktop| menu[Dropdown menu]
 91|    device -->|Mobile| sheet[Bottom sheet]
 92|    menu --> merge((.))
 93|    sheet --> merge
 94|    merge --> pick[Pick an item]
 95|    pick --> done([Item shown])
 96|    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
 97|```
 98|
 99|### Three outcomes
100|
101|```mermaid
102|flowchart TD
103|    start([Request sent]) --> result{Response?}
104|    result -->|Approved| done([Access granted])
105|    result -->|Rejected| reject([Reason shown])
106|    result -->|Needs info| ask[Ask for missing info]
107|    ask --> start
108|    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
109|```
110|
111|### A flow split across two diagrams
112|
113|Divide the ordered source list into groups of at most 9 nodes before the first Mermaid block, each group ending on a hand-off node that names it, so the split is read off the sources rather than a model that already overran. A flow over 9 nodes ends the first diagram on a named hand-off and starts the second diagram from the same name. Both diagrams go into the same file as two boards, read left to right: the second write passes the `fileKey` the first one used, and each board's `%% title:` carries its ordinal and its hand-off, such as `1. Sign up` and `2. Setup`. Every source step lands in one of the diagrams or is listed as left out under the provenance table.
114|
115|```mermaid
116|flowchart TD
117|    start([Sign up]) --> verify[Verify the email]
118|    verify --> profile[Fill in the profile]
119|    profile --> handoff([Continue to setup])
120|    style handoff fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
121|```
122|
123|```mermaid
124|flowchart TD
125|    handoff([Continue to setup]) --> connect[Connect an account]
126|    connect --> done([Dashboard shown])
127|    style done fill:#CDF4D3,stroke:#66D575
128|```
129|
130|---
131|
132|## 3. PROVENANCE TABLE
133|
134|One row per item, written in the intake before any Mermaid, beside the model and never on the board. An item is a node, a state, a participant, an entity, a task or an edge. An edge earns a row whenever it was inferred rather than read off a source, because a row kept only for an edge whose ends differ leaves an inferred connector unclassified.
135|
136|| Item | Kind | Source | Source class | Confidence | Rung |
137||---|---|---|---|---|---|
138|| start | node | `<screenshot file, Figma node or doc section>` | current behavior | high | stated |
139|| valid | node | `<source that states the check>` | current behavior | high | stated |
140|| start to valid | edge | `<neighbouring frames with no stated move>` | current behavior | medium | `<ladder step>` |
141|
142|The source class is one of current behavior, approved direction, proposal, retired material and unknown. A row marked proposal or unknown carries its status into the node label, or the node is left out.
143|
144|The confidence is `high`, `medium` or `low`. `high` is an item a source states, `medium` is an item one source implies and `low` is an item the ladder reached by joining two sources. Confidence is not the Brief's status, which says whether a row was captured, so the two sit on one item without repeating each other. The rung is the step of the inference ladder in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 that produced the row, and it reads `stated` when a source states the item outright.
145|
146|A `medium` or `low` row carries its uncertainty in the node label or is left out, so the board never shows a confident shape over a thin source. A board has no marker to hide, so the label is where the uncertainty lives.
147|
148|Where a frame name and the frame's visible heading differ, both are recorded in the row and the heading labels the node, because the heading is what the reader sees. The difference is a finding for the playback and is never resolved in the row.
149|
150|Below the table, list every source item that is in no diagram, each with its reason. This is the fidelity ledger sk-design-diagram asks for, so a split or a cut at a lower detail level is named here too:
151|
152|```text
153|Left out: <source item>, <reason, such as retired material, a split that ends before it or a cut at the simplified detail level>
154|```
155|
156|---
157|
158|## 4. REPLY SHAPE
159|
160|```text
161|<board URL>
162|Read-back: <counts the type's reference names, each as n of n>
163|Extensions: <n> of <n> pins, <n> of <n> legend stickies, <n> overlaps
164|Left out: <source item>, <reason>
165|Finding: <a read-back finding, a write warning, an open item or a question>
166|HVR self-scan: <n> hard blockers. Fixed: <terms>. Kept with reason: <terms>.
167|```
168|
169|The `Read-back:` counts follow the type: nodes, connectors and labelled decision exits for a user flow, lanes as well for a process, participants and messages for a sequence, states and transitions for a state diagram, entities, relationships and attributes for an ER diagram, and sections, tasks and milestones for a gantt chart. The `Extensions:` line appears only when the write added any, and the `Left out:` line only when the provenance table lists items left out, so the user sees what the board does not hold. When only a screenshot could be read, the read-back line ends with `, read visually`, because a picture cannot prove which nodes a connector joins. When the connector has no read tool, the line is `Read-back: not possible, the connector has no read tool`, and the board is never called done.
170|
171|These lines are the whole reply, and the self-scan is always the last. Each finding, warning, open item or question is one `Finding:` line, and nothing follows the self-scan. The playback of the settled rows runs before the model and the gate, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 8 sets out, and it never becomes a line here.
172|
173|---
174|
175|## 5. INTAKE QUESTIONS
176|
177|The type table in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3 reads as questions. Ask them as an interview before the model is written, in three rounds that depend on each other, because an answer in one round settles what the next round may ask.
178|
179|| Round | Asks | Settles |
180||---|---|---|
181|| One | The reader, the question and the outcome | Who the board is for, what it must answer and what the reader decides next |
182|| Two | Entry, exit and actors | Where the flow starts, where it ends and who takes each step |
183|| Three | Decisions, states, sources and class | Where the flow branches, which states exist, which source states each fact and what class that source holds |
184|
185|### Every question carries a reading and a recommendation
186|
187|A user who does not know an answer should still be able to accept one, so every question is put in this shape:
188|
189|```text
190|Reading: <what the sources already show for this question>
191|Question: <the one thing still open>
192|Recommended: <the answer the AI would take>
193|Why: <the one line of reason>
194|```
195|
196|- One to three questions per round and no later round while an earlier one is open
197|- Never a question a supplied source already answers, because that answer is stated as the reading instead
198|- A round closes when each of its questions is answered, accepted or corrected
199|
200|### A vague answer is asked again
201|
202|An answer that names nothing is asked once more with one probe from this set, and never with the same wording twice:
203|
204|- A concrete scenario, such as one example walked from the first click to the end
205|- An edge case, such as two of these arriving at once
206|- A contradiction, such as one source stating this and another stating the opposite
207|- A term, such as what one word means in this product
208|- A scale, such as how many of these exist on a busy day
209|- A failure mode, such as what the reader sees when one step fails
210|- A boundary, such as where this flow stops and another one begins
211|
212|### An unanswered question is never a dead end
213|
214|When the user skips a question or says they do not know, the AI takes the recommended answer. That fact is marked assumed in the Brief and named in the playback before the gate, so the user corrects it before anything is written. A row the user corrects is recorded as `corrected` and counts as settled. No later round asks it again.
</file-view>

 14|# FigJam Type - State
 15|
 16|A state diagram shows the states one thing can be in and what moves it between them: an order, a booking, a subscription, a review. It answers the questions a Product Owner gets asked most about status fields.
 17|
 18|**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, when the Flow route draws a state diagram
 19|**Purpose:** The grammar, rules, budget and read-back for a state diagram
 20|**Pairs With:** `assets/templates/state.md`
 21|
 22|---
 23|
 24|## 1. WHEN TO USE
 25|
 26|**The reader's question:** which states exist, what moves the thing between them, and what guards each move?
 27|
 28|- A lifecycle such as draft, review, published and archived
 29|- A status field whose values and allowed changes need agreeing before a story is written
 30|- A protocol or session with explicit states
 31|
 32|Use a process when people and steps are the subject, and a sequence when several parties exchange messages.
 33|
 34|---
 35|
 36|## 2. WHAT THE BOARD DRAWS
 37|
 38|```text
 39|stateDiagram-v2
 40|    direction LR
 41|    [*] --> Draft
 42|    Draft --> Review: submit
 43|    Review --> Draft: reject
 44|    Review --> Published: approve
 45|    Published --> [*]
 46|```
 47|
 48|- `[*]` starts and ends the machine, by the arrow's direction
 49|- A state is a word id, or an id with a description: `Pending: Waiting for payment`, or `state "Waiting for payment" as Pending`
 50|- A composite groups substates: `state Active { ... }`, with its own `[*]` entry and exit inside
 51|- `state Gate <<choice>>` branches on a condition, and `<<fork>>` and `<<join>>` split and rejoin parallel paths
 52|- `--` inside a composite splits it into regions that run at the same time
 53|
 54|On the board the first state takes the `entry` role, a state the machine ends from the `done` role and every other state the `neutral` role. The start and end are dots and a fork or join a bar, all in the `pseudo` role, and a choice is a small diamond in the `decision` role. `assets/figjam-design.md` names the swatch each role draws. Each composite is a tinted section named after it, around its substates.
 55|
 56|---
 57|
 58|## 3. RULES
 59|
 60|The check enforces:
 61|
 62|- **`stateDiagram-v2`,** never the legacy `stateDiagram`, running `LR` or `TB`, where `TD` is another name for `TB`
 63|- **No note and no styling.** The generated fallback reads the text inside a note and the names inside a style line as new states, so its board grows phantom boxes. The composer colours states by role itself, and notes are hybrid extensions
 64|- **Transitions written `-->`,** and the machine entered from `[*]`
 65|- **Every transition between two states carries a label,** the event that triggers it. A move into or out of `[*]`, a fork or a join may go without
 66|- **A choice has 2 or 3 exits,** each with a guard label
 67|- **Composites one level deep.** A composite inside a composite is its own diagram
 68|- **Transitions stay within their level.** Mermaid forbids a move into another composite's substate, so the move goes to or from the composite itself
 69|- **Every state has a transition,** and state ids are camelCase or PascalCase. A state whose name is more than one word, or carries a hyphen, takes its readable name as a description, such as `state "In stay" as InStay` or `state "No-show" as NoShow`, because the composer draws the id itself when a state has none
 70|- **At most 9 states and 12 transitions,** and never more than twice as many moves between states as states, the `[*]` entry and exit arrows aside, which sk-design-diagram reads as two machines drawn as one
 71|- The shared rules: labels of at most 40 characters, no emoji, markup or literal `\n`
 72|
 73|Judged by hand:
 74|
 75|- **States are nouns or adjectives,** such as `Confirmed`. Actions are transition labels, such as `pay`
 76|- **Labels follow `event [guard] / action`,** dropping the parts a move does not need, in one to three words where possible
 77|- **A move from any state, such as a timeout, is one transition from a composite,** never one from every state
 78|- **Mark terminal states with `--> [*]`** only when the thing really ends
 79|
 80|---
 81|
 82|## 4. BUDGET AND SPLITTING
 83|
 84|Over budget, split by phase, such as booking and stay, or by entity. A coarse machine with one composite per phase plus one diagram per composite reads better than one deep machine. At `Meeting screen` distance transition labels drop to 32 characters. At `Wall` distance the budget drops to 6 states and 8 transitions, with labels at 25 characters, as the reading distance dial in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets out.
 85|
 86|---
 87|
 88|## 5. COLOUR, ZONES AND NOTES
 89|
 90|None in the model. The composer colours the first and final states and the pseudo-states by role, and composites are the zones. A grouping the model does not hold, such as every error state, is a composite when the states share a way out, and otherwise a note. A self-transition can render tight against its state, so tell the user they can drag its loop in FigJam if it crowds. A `%% focus: <id>` line may name the one node the first glance lands on. It is a comment, so the model stays styleless.
 91|
 92|---
 93|
 94|## 6. WRITING THE BOARD
 95|
 96|`scripts/compose_board.py` composes the model and one `use_figma` call draws the board, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 6 sets out. On the generated fallback, `generate_diagram` takes `name`, `mermaidSyntax` and `userIntent`, and no `useArchitectureLayoutCode`. The `fj` route cannot draw a state diagram.
 97|
 98|---
 99|
100|## 7. READ-BACK
101|
102|Count states, transitions and labelled transitions, and check every guard on a choice. A composite draws as the section around its substates, so it counts as a state by its section name.
103|
104|```text
105|Read-back: 6 of 6 states, 8 of 8 transitions, 6 of 6 transitions labelled
106|```
107|
108|---
109|
110|## 8. PATTERNS AND EXAMPLE
111|
112|- `assets/templates/state.md` holds a lifecycle, a composite and a choice
113|- `assets/examples/state-roamstay-booking.md` draws a booking's status field from a product doc
</file-view>

 14|
 15|# FigJam Diagram Quality Rubric
 16|
 17|The script checks what a script can see. This rubric is the rest: whether the diagram should exist, whether every node earns its place and whether the reader can trust what lands on the board. Walk it after the check passes and before the write gate.
 18|
 19|**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, on every Flow route before the write gate
 20|**Purpose:** The judgement pass between the pre-write check and the gate
 21|**Scope:** The model, the provenance table, the planned extensions and, after the write, the board and the reply
 22|
 23|---
 24|
 25|## 1. TYPE FIT
 26|
 27|- [ ] The type answers the reader's question, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3 maps it
 28|- [ ] A table, a list or a paragraph would not do the same job. If it would, say so and offer that instead
 29|- [ ] The type's reference in `references/types/` was loaded and its judged-by-hand rules were applied
 30|- [ ] A request for a kind Flow Mode does not draw was answered with the nearest type it does draw, or a plain no
 31|
 32|---
 33|
 34|## 2. THE REMOVE TEST
 35|
 36|sk-design-diagram's highest-quality move is usually deletion. A diagram is done when nothing can be removed.
 37|
 38|The remove test runs on the outline before the first Mermaid block, because a step cut from a list of steps costs a sentence and the same step cut from a drawn diagram costs a redraw. This section is the third rung of the challenge ladder in `references/flow-mode.md` Section 3, so the two rungs above it are asked first: what the board must not do, and whether a list, a table or a paragraph would serve the reader better.
 39|
 40|- [ ] The `userIntent` sentence was agreed in the sparring and is the first line of the outline, rather than composed at the write call
 41|- [ ] The remove test ran on the outline, one line per node and edge, before any layout was judged
 42|- [ ] An unanswered sparring proposal is marked assumed and named in the playback before the gate
 43|- [ ] No node can be removed without the reader losing a step they need
 44|- [ ] Every node serves the `userIntent` sentence, or it is cut and named under `Left out:`
 45|- [ ] No two nodes always travel together. If they do, they are one node
 46|- [ ] No connector restates what the layout already shows
 47|- [ ] No label repeats what the shape already says
 48|- [ ] No diagram carries the same label on four or more connectors. Cut them all, or keep one where the label says something the shape cannot. Decision exits and sequence messages are exempt, and an architecture renames each edge instead, as its type reference sets out
 49|- [ ] The remove test ran on the outline before the first Mermaid block, so no node was drawn only to be cut
 50|- [ ] The diagram sits inside its budget, or was split, and every cut is named under `Left out:`
 51|
 52|---
 53|
 54|## 3. SIGNAL
 55|
 56|The marked node is chosen against a target written down first. A board judged only against itself cannot catch a second focal object, such as a title that repeats the claim the marked node was meant to carry. Three lines are written before the first Mermaid block:
 57|
 58|1. **First glance.** The one claim, decision or object that should win within two seconds
 59|2. **Second glance.** The evidence or relationship that advances it
 60|3. **Last glance.** The risk, the metadata or the appendix that stays available without competing
 61|
 62|Those three lines travel into the gate, so the marked node is chosen from them and the reply can say what should win. After the first glance, filled shapes and their keyed fills outweigh connector labels and text in the overview, so the lines name a filled group such as the gray end states before the labels between them.
 63|
 64|- [ ] One accent on a user flow or a process, on the node a reader would keep if they could keep only one, never the node that comes first. The goal, a failure end, a decision and the one step in focus are the candidates, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 3 sets out. Two that tie mean the diagram splits
 65|- [ ] The three glance lines were written before the model and named in the gate
 66|- [ ] On a user flow or a process the first glance is the accented node, marked by the one `style` line the check requires, and the gate names it. On any other type it is the node, message or task a `%% focus:` line names, or, when the model has none, whatever the layout shows first, and the gate says which. The first glance is one node, message or task, never a group such as the end states, and when the layout would show another first, a `%% focus:` line marks it, so the gate never promises a first glance the board does not show. It is the claim the reader came for rather than the node the flow reaches first, and nothing the second or last glance owns competes with it
 67|- [ ] No title repeats the focal claim, so one idea carries one focal object. Where the title already states the claim, the marked node carries the evidence, the consequence or the next move
 68|- [ ] The title names what the reader is looking at, the subtitle says in one sentence who reads it and why, and the source line names the sources and what was left out
 69|- [ ] Shape and label carry the meaning on their own, so the diagram reads in greyscale
 70|- [ ] The key the composer draws names every kind, line and arrow the board shows and nothing else, and no note adds a second key beside it
 71|- [ ] Every zone carries a name a reader can see, and zones group what belongs together rather than marking a position
 72|- [ ] Every label uses the product's or the source's own words. Proper nouns are never renamed
 73|- [ ] The naming fits the audience: exact component names for engineers, plain verbs for a mixed team, capabilities and outcomes for leadership
 74|- [ ] Nothing was invented to fill a lane, a slot or a gap. A missing step is asked about or named, never guessed
 75|
 76|---
 77|
 78|## 4. PROVENANCE
 79|
 80|- [ ] Every node has a row in the provenance table naming its source and its source class
 81|- [ ] Nothing marked proposal or unknown is drawn as current behavior. Its status sits in its label, or it is left out
 82|- [ ] Every causal edge is stated by its sources from both ends. An edge one source states and another contradicts is a finding, not a connector
 83|- [ ] A contradicted item leaves a trace the reader can see. It sits in the reply's `Left out:` line with both sources and the reason, or the one question that asks which source governs settled it. Nothing is removed in silence and no extra line is invented for it
 84|
 85|---
 86|
 87|## 5. THE CHECK AND THE GATE
 88|
 89|- [ ] `scripts/flow_check.py` printed `PASSED` for the model file, with the type each diagram was read as
 90|- [ ] The measures printed beside the counts were read: the widest rank, the longest path, the connectors per step, the average label length and the crossing pairs, against the budgets `scripts/figjam_checks/layout.py` sets
 91|- [ ] A measure out of band was fixed in the model rather than on the board and the check rerun after the change, because the composer owns the layout and a tangled shape is never rearranged after the write
 92|- [ ] `scripts/compose_board.py` printed `COMPOSED` for every diagram, with the counts the read-back will look for
 93|- [ ] The gate message names the plan, the file, what will be written, any planned extensions, the calls the write will spend and the rollback
 94|- [ ] On the generated fallback, an architecture call carries `useArchitectureLayoutCode`, and no other type carries it
 95|
 96|---
 97|
 98|## 6. THE BOARD
 99|
100|After the write, before the reply:
101|
102|- [ ] The read-back counts match the model, as the type's reference sets them out
103|- [ ] Each provenance row whose class is not current behavior or whose edge is inferred was re-read against its source before the gate, and the row records the reason. A row that quotes a source line was not re-read
104|- [ ] The write returned no warning, and its counts match the counts the model expects
105|- [ ] The `COMPOSED` line named the design the board was drawn in, and each `DESIGN` warning it counted became a `Finding:` line naming the token and the shipped value the board used instead
106|- [ ] The overview is the screenshot the composing call returned, and `get_figjam` supplies the outline with a screenshot of each node
107|- [ ] A node that needs its own view is read with `get_screenshot` and a node id from that read, because the tool fails without one
108|- [ ] Two screenshots of the board were taken for this pass: one of the whole board in a single frame and one at 100% zoom. Composition is judged on the overview, because a crossing and a crowded label are invisible at reading size
109|- [ ] The overview reads in the order the model plans, and that order was written down before the first screenshot
110|- [ ] The overview shows no connector crossing another, no connector or label on a zone title, no two edges sharing a trunk the model draws apart and no two labels touching
111|- [ ] No edge runs through a zone it neither starts nor ends in. Edges that only arrive may share one magnet and then lie together for no more than 200 pixels
112|- [ ] One screenshot of the diagram shows no stretched shape, no label cut off and no overlap with existing board content
113|- [ ] Every gap a note or a person placed falls in one of the three bands `references/style-guide.md` Section 7 states, and two unrelated groups sit no closer than the text blocks inside a card
114|- [ ] Each zone holds its own nodes and no other, and no zone overlaps another
115|- [ ] The same screenshot shows no connector crossing and no edge that reads as joining the wrong node. Each edge is followed by eye from end to end, because a connector count does not prove that a route is clear
116|- [ ] Every colour on the board matches its entry in the key, the marked node sits where Section 3 places it, and the board answers the `userIntent` sentence without the model beside it
117|- [ ] Every fill on the board resolves to a role in the active design, as `assets/figjam-design.md` holds it, no zone tint shares a hue with a kind inside it or with the accent, and no note added a colour the design does not name
118|- [ ] The marked node reads first, and no other node competes with it
119|- [ ] A screenshot finding is reported, and it is fixed only by reshaping the model and composing again after a yes, inside the two-attempt bound `references/flow-mode.md` Section 9 sets
120|- [ ] Each extension landed where planned and covers no composed node's label
121|- [ ] Nothing was moved, resized or restyled after the write
122|- [ ] Every finding below full marks names the label it sits on, where it sits in the frame, and one fix, which is a model change composed again after a yes or a named composer limit the writer cannot move
123|
124|---
125|
126|## 7. THE DESIGN RUBRIC
127|
128|The checklists above decide whether a board may ship. The design rubric scores how well it reads, so two boards of the same model, or a board before and after a change, can be compared on something firmer than a glance. Score the overview screenshot on nine criteria, each 0, 1 or 2, for a total out of 18. A criterion scores 2 when it holds everywhere on the board, 1 when it holds with one named exception and 0 when it fails in two places or more.
129|
130|| Criterion | Scores 2 when |
131||---|---|
132|| Frame and entry | The board is one framed area with a title, a one-sentence subtitle and one obvious place to start reading |
133|| Reading order | The flow runs in one direction, the main route sits on one straight line and every branch sits beside it rather than across it |
134|| Colour by meaning | Every colour names a kind the key explains, and nothing is coloured for looks or by position |
135|| Grouping | Zones, lanes or composite states group what belongs together, each carries a visible name and neighbouring tints differ |
136|| Legibility | At overview zoom every label reads, no text is cut off or crowded and shapes of one kind share one size |
137|| Connector clarity | No connector crosses another or runs through a node or a zone title, two edges never lie on one stretch long enough to carry a label, every label sits on its own edge and clear of every other line and every end joins its node cleanly |
138|| Key and source | The key names every mark and nothing else, and the source line names the sources and what was left out |
139|| Proportion | The board reads wider than tall or close to square, with no tall strip, no large empty region and margins on the grid |
140|| Matches the active design | Every kind draws the pair its role names in `assets/figjam-design.md`, the title block and type sizes match every other board, the key lists its entries in the design's order with the focus last, every line takes the design's look and no zone tint shares a hue with a kind inside it |
141|
142|Every score below 2 names the label or the zone it sits on and one fix, in the same shape Section 6 asks of a finding. A comparison between two boards scores both on the same nine criteria and reports both totals, criterion by criterion, so a gain on one criterion never hides a loss on another.
143|
144|---
145|
146|## 8. THE REPLY
147|
148|- [ ] The board URL first, then the `Read-back:` line, then any `Extensions:` and `Left out:` lines, then any `Finding:` lines, then the `HVR self-scan:` line, with no text after it
149|- [ ] No sentence or key entry ties a colour or a zone tint to a team
150|- [ ] A mismatch is reported as measured, and the board is never called done on one
151|- [ ] No file was written to `export/`, and no Mermaid, HTML, SVG or PNG file was left behind
</file-view>

 16|# FigJam Diagram Style Guide
 17|
 18|The rules for colour, type and spacing on a FigJam board. The composer in `assets/compose-board.js` draws every board in the design `assets/figjam-design.md` holds, which ships as the tables below record, and every hex a model, a design or a note extension uses comes from the palette in Section 3. `scripts/flow_check.py` refuses any other.
 19|
 20|**Loading Condition:** CONDITIONAL, before the gate on every Flow route, and when a model or a note extension uses colour
 21|**Purpose:** Names the colour each kind draws in, the type scale, the grid, the palette pairs the check accepts and the measured contrast record
 22|**Scope:** The composed board, Mermaid `style`, `classDef` and `linkStyle` colours, sticky and pin colours for notes, and the contrast record the self-test re-measures
 23|
 24|---
 25|
 26|## 1. OVERVIEW
 27|
 28|sk-design-diagram owns a skinnable palette with semantic roles and a record of where each value comes from. A FigJam board already has a palette of its own, and a colour the board recognises as a palette swatch can be recoloured from FigJam's colour picker by anyone on the board. So this guide does not skin the board. It picks FigJam's own pairs, gives each kind of node one of them and records what each pair measures.
 29|
 30|Three rules carry the board:
 31|
 32|- **Colour by meaning.** A kind fixes a node's shape and colour together, so a goal is light green and a decision light yellow on every board, whichever type draws them. A colour never marks a position in the layout and is never picked for looks
 33|- **The key names every colour.** The composer draws one key under the diagram, with a sample of every kind, line and arrow the board uses and nothing else, so a reader never meets a colour the board does not explain
 34|- **Colour never carries meaning alone.** Most kinds also differ by shape, such as a diamond for a decision or a cylinder for a data store. Where two kinds share a shape and differ only by colour, such as a goal and an exit, the label names the outcome and the key names both, so a reader who cannot tell the fills apart still reads the board
 35|
 36|The board's look is a design a team can change. `assets/figjam-design.md` holds it as tokens: the palette pair each colour role draws, the role each kind takes, the accent, the type sizes, the line colours, the zone tints and the words on the key. The tables below record the shipped design. A design that changes a token changes the board and not this guide, and a token that breaks a gate in Section 4 or a floor in that file's Section 7 falls back to its shipped value with a warning.
 37|
 38|The board carries one accent, by default a heavy pink outline on the node, message or task the first glance names. A user flow or a process marks it with a `style` line and the check refuses a model that has none. The other five types may name it with a `%% focus:` line. A `style` line does not colour a node for the board. It tells the composer what the node means, as Section 3 sets out.
 39|
 40|---
 41|
 42|## 2. KINDS
 43|
 44|The composer reads each node's kind from the model: its shape, its place in the flow, its lane, its stereotype or its `style` line. The kind fixes the shape and the pair, and the key names it in the words below.
 45|
 46|### Flows and processes
 47|
 48|| Kind | Shape | Colour | Key | Read from |
 49||---|---|---|---|---|
 50|| Start | Rounded rectangle | Light blue | Where it starts | A stadium node no edge enters |
 51|| Screen or step | Rounded rectangle | White | Screen or step, or Step on a process | A plain node |
 52|| Decision | Diamond | Light yellow | Decision | A rhombus |
 53|| Goal | Rounded rectangle | Light green | Goal reached | A styled end, or the end the longest path reaches when none is styled |
 54|| Exit | Rounded rectangle | Light orange | Leaves the flow | Every other unstyled end |
 55|| Error | Rounded rectangle | Light red | Error or blocked | An end styled with the light red pair |
 56|| Focus | Rounded rectangle | Light pink, 8 pixel outline | In focus | A styled step that is none of the kinds above |
 57|| Merge | 24 pixel dot | Dark gray | Paths join | A circle |
 58|| Data store | Cylinder | Light violet | Data store | A cylinder |
 59|| Sub-process | Predefined process | White | Sub-process | A subroutine |
 60|| Input or output | Parallelogram | Light teal | Input or output | A parallelogram |
 61|
 62|An exit and an error sit beside the main line rather than on it, so the longest route to the goal stays one straight line.
 63|
 64|The accent is not a kind. A styled goal, error, decision or any other node keeps the kind and fill it has and takes the pink outline on top, so a goal stays green and reads first. Only a styled step has no kind of its own to keep, so it is drawn light pink. The key adds `In focus` whenever the board carries an accent, and its sample is drawn as the marked node is, its own kind under the pink outline, so a goal in focus shows a green sample and a styled step a light pink one.
 65|
 66|### Architecture
 67|
 68|The lane a part sits in fixes its kind: a client is light teal, an edge or gateway light blue, a service white, a queue or stream an orange queue shape, a data store a violet cylinder and an outside system light gray.
 69|
 70|### State, ER, sequence and gantt
 71|
 72|| Kind | Shape | Colour | Key |
 73||---|---|---|---|
 74|| Initial and final pseudo-state | 32 pixel dot, the final one ringed | Charcoal | Start, End |
 75|| First state, a state, final state | Rounded rectangle | Light blue, white, light gray | First state, State, Final state |
 76|| Choice | 56 pixel diamond | Light yellow | Choice |
 77|| Fork or join | 16 by 96 pixel bar | Charcoal | Fork or join |
 78|| Entity | Card with its fields | White | Entity |
 79|| Participant | Rounded rectangle, drawn again smaller at the foot of its lifeline | White | Participant |
 80|| Planned, in progress, done, critical | Bar, the planned one outlined in the connector gray and the critical one with a heavier outline and `, critical` after its length | White, light blue, light gray, light red | Planned, In progress, Done, Critical, heavy outline |
 81|| Milestone | 32 pixel diamond | Light yellow | Milestone |
 82|
 83|A sequence numbers every message with a pin in the `marker` role, violet as shipped, beside its sender's lifeline, and its key names the pin `Step number`.
 84|
 85|### Lines and zones
 86|
 87|| Element | Colour | Notes |
 88||---|---|---|
 89|| Connector | Gray `#757575`, 2 pixels | Dashed for an optional or proposed edge, and for an async or outside call on an architecture |
 90|| Request, reply | Gray solid and gray dashed, both with a closed head | Sequence |
 91|| Async message, async reply | Blue `#3DADFF`, solid or dashed, with an open head | Sequence |
 92|| Lifeline | Light gray `#B3B3B3`, dashed | Sequence |
 93|| Accent | Pink `#F849C1`, 8 pixels around a node or bar and 4 pixels along a sequence message | The only pink and the only heavy line on a board |
 94|| Relationship | Gray, solid when identifying and dashed when not, no arrow | ER, with the cardinality in the label |
 95|| Zone | A section in a light tint, named in 24 pixel type | Tints cycle blue, orange, teal, yellow and violet. A zone skips a tint any kind inside it draws and the tint of any zone beside it, so a tint never hides its members and two neighbouring zones never read as one. A gantt section takes its band the same way |
 96|| Key | A light gray section under the diagram and as wide as it | One sample per mark the board uses, in one order on every board of a type with the focus last, wrapping onto a new row at the diagram's edge |
 97|| Board | A white section around everything | Named after the title |
 98|
 99|---
100|
101|## 3. PALETTE
102|
103|### Accent and lane pairs
104|
105|The check accepts exactly the pairs in this record. Each fill takes only the stroke FigJam pairs it with, and a connector takes either the stroke or nothing. The lane pair is Figma's own suggestion for a diagram's one container, and it never counts as the accent. The composer draws every kind from the same pairs, with white for the plain kinds, charcoal for the pseudo-states, dark gray for the merge dot and the violet label preset for the pins. The light pink pair is the accent's and no kind draws it. A design may give the accent another pair, and then that pair is the accent's alone.
106|
107|The two ratio columns are measured: dark text on the fill against the 4.5:1 text gate, and the stroke on a white canvas against the 3.0:1 mark gate. `scripts/flow_check.py --self-test` re-measures every row and fails when a number or a pair drifts.
108|
109|<!-- FIGJAM_PALETTE:BEGIN -->
110|| Role | Fill | Stroke | Text on fill | Stroke on canvas |
111||---|---|---|---|---|
112|| Light green | `#CDF4D3` | `#66D575` | 13.87:1 | 1.85:1 |
113|| Light teal | `#C6FAF6` | `#5AD8CC` | 14.61:1 | 1.73:1 |
114|| Light blue | `#C2E5FF` | `#3DADFF` | 12.66:1 | 2.44:1 |
115|| Light violet | `#DCCCFF` | `#874FFF` | 11.21:1 | 4.57:1 |
116|| Light pink | `#FFC2EC` | `#F849C1` | 11.26:1 | 3.13:1 |
117|| Light red | `#FFCDC2` | `#FF7556` | 11.72:1 | 2.65:1 |
118|| Light orange | `#FFE0C2` | `#FF9E42` | 13.25:1 | 2.05:1 |
119|| Light yellow | `#FFECBD` | `#FFC943` | 14.28:1 | 1.53:1 |
120|| Light gray | `#D9D9D9` | `#B3B3B3` | 11.81:1 | 2.1:1 |
121|| Lane | `#F5F5F5` | `#B3B3B3` | 15.29:1 | 2.1:1 |
122|<!-- FIGJAM_PALETTE:END -->
123|
124|### What a `style` line means
125|
126|A user flow or a process may carry one `style` line, or several on nodes that share one pair. The composer reads it as meaning, not as paint:
127|
128|| Where it sits | Pair | What the board shows |
129||---|---|---|
130|| On an end | Light red | An error, in light red, with the pink outline |
131|| On an end | Any other pair | The goal, in light green, with the pink outline, and the spine runs to it |
132|| On a decision | Any pair | The decision keeps its light yellow diamond and takes the pink outline |
133|| On a step | Any pair | That step in focus, in light pink |
134|
135|Pick the node the board exists to explain first, then the line that says what it is. A user flow and a process each need one such line, because the board has no other way to say what the first glance is, and the check refuses a model without one. With no end styled, the end the longest path reaches is still the goal and the others leave the flow, but the goal then carries no outline. A `linkStyle` line passes the check and changes nothing on a composed board, because a connector's colour belongs to its kind, and it never counts as the accent. An architecture, a sequence, a state diagram, an ER diagram and a gantt chart take no `style` line, because their kinds already carry their colour, and the check refuses styling on an architecture.
136|
137|### The accent
138|
139|The first glance is the one node, message or task a reader should see within two seconds, and the accent is how the board says so. Three measures keep it first:
140|
141|- **A hue no kind uses.** The light pink pair belongs to the accent alone and every kind draws another pair. The nearest kind hues, light red at 52 degrees and light violet at 60, sit well clear of the accent's 319
142|- **Weight as well as colour.** A marked node or bar takes an 8 pixel outline against 2 for every other node and 4 for a critical bar, and a marked message takes 4 pixels against 2. On a greyscale copy pink and light blue are both just grey, so the line is what tells them apart. Weight times contrast on white puts 25.0 on the accent against 4.9 on the start pill and 12.6 on the heaviest other mark, the ring of an end state
143|- **The mark gate.** The pink stroke measures 3.13:1 on white, which only violet also clears, so it is the one outline on the board that holds at overview zoom
144|
145|The start pill keeps its light blue, because at those weights it cannot outweigh the accent in colour or in greyscale. What carries the accent depends on the type:
146|
147|| Type | What carries the accent | How the model says so |
148||---|---|---|
149|| User flow, process | A node: a step, a decision, the goal or an error end | A `style` line, which the check requires |
150|| Architecture, state, ER | A node | `%% focus: <id>`, optional |
151|| Sequence | A message | `%% focus: <number>`, the message's place in the order, optional |
152|| Gantt | A task or a milestone | `%% focus: <id or name>`, optional |
153|
154|A `%% focus:` line is a comment, so the Mermaid stays plain. It names one thing, and a second line, a name that matches nothing or a line on a user flow or a process is refused. Where a type carries no focus line the first glance is whatever the layout shows first, and the gate says so. A planned first glance is one thing, never a group such as the end states, and when the layout would show another first, the model names it with a focus line rather than promise a glance the board does not give.
155|
156|### Note palettes
157|
158|The composer and a note extension both set colour through the Plugin API, where FigJam recognises a colour as a palette swatch only when each channel is written as `hex/255`. A rounded decimal makes it a custom colour that the colour picker no longer offers.
159|
160|| Node | Palette |
161||---|---|
162|| Sticky | White `#FFFFFF`, gray `#E6E6E6`, green `#B3EFBD`, teal `#B3F4EF`, blue `#A8DAFF`, violet `#D3BDFF`, pink `#FFA8DB`, red `#FFB8A8`, orange `#FFD3A8`, yellow `#FFE299` |
163|| Section | White `#FFFFFF`, light gray `#F9F9F9`, light green `#EBFFEE`, light teal `#F1FEFD`, light blue `#F5FBFF`, light violet `#F8F5FF`, light pink `#FFF0FA`, light red `#FFF5F5`, light orange `#FFF7F0`, light yellow `#FFFBF0` |
164|| Label | Violet fill `#874FFF`, stroke `#5427B4`, white text, the one preset for numbered pins |
165|
166|Sticky colours keep FigJam's usual meanings: blue for discussion, yellow for a question, green for a positive, pink for a concern, red for a blocker and teal for a decision. One sticky colour per legend is the default, because the numbers already tell the stickies apart.
167|
168|---
169|
170|## 4. GATES
171|
172|| Gate | Threshold | Applies to |
173||---|---|---|
174|| Text on fill | 4.5:1 | Charcoal `#1E1E1E` on every fill the check accepts |
175|| Mark on canvas | 3.0:1 | A stroke that carries meaning, measured on a white canvas |
176|| Text on mark | 4.5:1 | The white digit on a label pin: 4.57:1 on violet `#874FFF` |
177|
178|### Recorded departures
179|
180|| Departure | Measures | Note |
181||---|---|---|
182|| Seven strokes on the canvas | 1.53:1 to 2.65:1 | Every stroke but violet and pink sits under the mark gate. They are FigJam's own pairs, kept so a reader can recolour them from the picker, and the check never lets colour carry meaning alone |
183|| The lane stroke `#B3B3B3` | 2.1:1 | A lane outline is a container edge, not a mark, and its label names it |
184|| Figma's blue label example | Not used | Its white digit on `#3DADFF` measures 2.44:1, under the text gate, so the label pin takes the violet preset |
185|| The saturated fills | Not accepted | FigJam sets white text on a saturated fill, which measures 1.85:1 on `#66D575`. Mermaid cannot set a text colour, and the generator's text colour on a saturated fill was never observed, so the check refuses them |
186|
187|The canvas is measured as white. FigJam's canvas is near white with a dot grid, and its exact value was not measured, so a stroke reads a little weaker on the board than the column says.
188|
189|---
190|
191|## 5. TYPE AND GRID
192|
193|sk-design-diagram's type ramp and grid carry over, because the composer sets the font itself. Every board uses one family at one scale, Inter unless a design names another. A family FigJam cannot load falls back to Inter with a warning:
194|
195|| Text | Size | Weight |
196||---|---|---|
197|| Title | 64 | Bold |
198|| Subtitle | 28 | Regular, wrapped at the diagram's width between 960 and 1440 pixels and then narrowed while it keeps its number of lines, so its lines come out even |
199|| Zone and key names | 24 | Semi Bold |
200|| Node label | 20 | Medium |
201|| Edge label, key entry, source line | 18 | Medium on a connector, Regular elsewhere |
202|| Entity field | 16 | Regular |
203|| Gantt bar length, step pin | 14 | Medium |
204|
205|Every position and size sits on an 8 pixel grid. A shape grows from its kind's base size until its label fits inside it, with a 32 pixel inset in a round shape whose text FigJam clips to the inscribed box, and every shape of one kind on a board takes the size of the largest, so a rank reads as one row.
206|
207|The scale is tuned for a laptop at overview zoom. Reading distance does not change it, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets out, and buys fewer nodes and shorter labels instead.
208|
209|A design re-maps meanings onto the pairs in Section 3 and never adds a colour. A board is shared and recoloured in FigJam, so a brand palette would turn every swatch into a custom colour. A brand colour asked for by name is a hand edit after the write, and the reply says it is off-palette.
210|
211|---
212|
213|## 6. WHAT HOLDS THE RECORD
214|
215|- `scripts/figjam_checks/common.py` holds the pairs the check accepts
216|- `assets/figjam-design.md` holds the design a board is drawn in, and `scripts/figjam_checks/design.py` reads it, checks every token against its floor and sends the composer only what differs from the built-in design
217|- `assets/compose-board.js` holds the built-in design, the swatches, the tints and the shapes, and `scripts/compose_board.py --self-test` measures the accent's hue, weight and ink on every board it composes and fails when the design file leaves out a token or breaks a floor
218|- `scripts/compose_board.py --design-check` prints the resolved design with its measured ratios and names every design warning
219|- The self-test fails when the record above names a pair the check does not accept, or the check accepts one the record does not name
220|- The self-test re-measures both ratio columns of every row and fails on any drift
221|
222|---
223|
224|## 7. SPACING
225|
226|Colour tells a reader what belongs together, but space tells them first. A reader groups what sits close before reading a label, so a board that spaces every gap the same reads as one flat field and its own structure disappears.
227|
228|| Band | Gap | What the gap separates |
229||---|---|---|
230|| One thought | 60 to 92 pixels | Two nodes a reader takes as one step or one idea |
231|| Same topic | 200 to 400 pixels | Two groups the board discusses one after the other |
232|| Another part of the board | 1000 pixels or more | Content that answers a different question |
233|
234|Two rules follow from the bands:
235|
236|- Two unrelated groups are never closer than the text blocks inside a card, so the gap between groups always reads wider than the gap within one
237|- A wrapper is larger than the group's own internal gap and smaller than the gap to the next group, so its edge never falls on a neighbour
238|

 15|# FigJam Board Design
 16|
 17|> FigJam's own palette with one meaning per colour, one pink first glance and Inter at seven sizes. Flat, light and drawn on an 8 pixel grid.
 18|
 19|This file is the style every board `assets/compose-board.js` draws. Change a token in the json block in Section 8 and every board composed after it follows. Nothing else needs editing. `scripts/compose_board.py` reads the block, sends the composer only the tokens that differ from its built-in design and names every token it could not use.
 20|
 21|---
 22|
 23|## 1. OVERVIEW
 24|
 25|A board is drawn from FigJam's own palette, so anyone on it can recolour a node from FigJam's picker later. A design never adds a colour. It chooses which FigJam pair carries which meaning.
 26|
 27|Three layers carry a colour from this file to a node:
 28|
 29|- **Swatches** are FigJam's own pairs, each a fill, a stroke and a text colour, and its light section tints. The block lists them as reference, and they stay as FigJam ships them
 30|- **Roles** say what a colour means, such as `goal` or `decision`, and each names one swatch. This is the layer a team restyles
 31|- **Kinds** are what a model draws, such as a decision or a data store. Each kind names one role and the words its key entry shows, and its shape stays the composer's
 32|
 33|So `"goal": "lightTeal"` turns every goal on every board teal and the key says so, while the shapes, the layout and the routing stay as they are. The board is flat: no shadow, no gradient and no fill on the board itself beyond white.
 34|
 35|---
 36|
 37|## 2. COLOUR ROLES
 38|
 39|| Role | Swatch | What it marks | Drawn by |
 40||---|---|---|---|
 41|| `entry` | Light blue | Where a reader starts | A flow's start, a state diagram's first state |
 42|| `neutral` | White | An ordinary step | Screens, steps, states, services, sub-processes, entities, participants and planned bars |
 43|| `goal` | Light green | The outcome the flow exists for | A flow's goal |
 44|| `exit` | Light orange | A way out of the flow | An exit end |
 45|| `error` | Light red | An error or a block | An error end, a critical gantt bar |
 46|| `decision` | Light yellow | A choice, or a point a plan reaches | Decisions, state choices, milestones |
 47|| `store` | Light violet | Data at rest | Data stores |
 48|| `io` | Light teal | Input or output | Input and output steps |
 49|| `client` | Light teal | An app or a client | Architecture clients |
 50|| `gateway` | Light blue | The edge of a system | Architecture gateways |
 51|| `queue` | Light orange | A queue or a stream | Architecture queues |
 52|| `external` | Light gray | A system outside the board's scope | Architecture outside systems |
 53|| `inProgress` | Light blue | Work under way | Gantt bars in progress |
 54|| `done` | Light gray | Work finished | Gantt done bars, a state diagram's final states |
 55|| `pseudo` | Charcoal | A state machine's own marks | Start and end dots, fork and join bars |
 56|| `junction` | Dark gray | Paths that join | A flow's merge dot |
 57|| `marker` | Violet | A numbered pin | A sequence's step numbers |
 58|
 59|Light blue serves three roles but never two on one board. A flow and a state diagram start in it, an architecture marks its gateways in it and a gantt chart its work in progress, and the key names the one a board uses. Light teal, light orange and light gray split the same way, by diagram type.
 60|
 61|---
 62|
 63|## 3. THE ACCENT
 64|
 65|The accent marks the one node, message or task a reader should see first. It is a pair no role draws, light pink by default, drawn as an `accent.node` outline of 8 pixels around a node or bar and an `accent.message` line of 4 pixels along a sequence message. A user flow or a process names it with a `style` line and the other types with `%% focus:`, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 3 sets out.
 66|
 67|It keeps first place by three measures, which Section 7 holds every edit to:
 68|
 69|- Its stroke clears 3:1 on white
 70|- Its hue sits 45 degrees or more from every role a kind draws, every tint in the zone cycle and every line colour and the key's tint
 71|- Its outline outweighs every other mark: heavier than the 6 pixel ring of an end state on a node, and heavier than the lines on a message
 72|
 73|---
 74|
 75|## 4. KINDS AND THE KEY
 76|
 77|Each kind in the `kind` group names its role and its key words. `focus` names no role, because it draws the accent's own pair. The key shows one sample per kind, line and arrow the board draws, the kinds in the composer's own order, which reordering the `kind` group does not change, then the lines, the arrows, the step pin and the focus last. It is as wide as the diagram, and an entry that would run past that edge starts a new row.
 78|
 79|The `key` group holds the key's own words: its title, the step pin's entry and one entry per line style and sequence arrow. Its `tint` is the section tint the key sits on.
 80|
 81|---
 82|
 83|## 5. TYPE
 84|
 85|| Token | Default | Weight | Where it is used |
 86||---|---|---|---|
 87|| `title` | 64 | Bold | The board's title |
 88|| `subtitle` | 28 | Regular | The line under the title, wrapped between 960 and 1440 pixels into even lines |
 89|| `zone` | 24 | Semi Bold | Zone names and the key's title |
 90|| `node` | 20 | Medium | Node labels and entity names |
 91|| `label` | 18 | Medium on a connector, Regular elsewhere | Edge labels, key entries, gantt axis and task names, the source line |
 92|| `field` | 16 | Regular | Entity fields |
 93|| `small` | 14 | Medium | Gantt bar lengths and step pins |
 94|
 95|`family` names the face. The board loads its Medium, Regular, Semi Bold and Bold styles, taking Semi Bold under either name FigJam gives it, `Semi Bold` or `SemiBold`. When a style will not load, the board is set in Inter and the composer's warnings say so, so pick a family that carries all four.
 96|
 97|---
 98|
 99|## 6. LINES AND ZONES
100|
101|| Token | Default | Draws |
102||---|---|---|
103|| `line.color` | `#757575` | Every connector, and a sequence's requests and replies |
104|| `line.async` | `#3DADFF` | A sequence's async messages and replies |
105|| `line.lifeline` | `#B3B3B3` | A sequence's lifelines |
106|| `line.weight` | 2 | Every line but the accent's |
107|
108|A line colour is one of the colours the swatch block holds, any fill, stroke or text, so it stays on FigJam's palette.
109|
110|`zone.cycle` lists the section tints zones and gantt sections take in turn. Each takes the first tint along the cycle that no node inside it draws and that no zone beside it took, within two zone gaps on any side. An orange exit never sits in an orange zone and two neighbouring zones never read as one, however the layout placed them. When no tint keeps both rules, a zone keeps the neighbour rule, repeats a member's hue and the composer's warnings say so. Pink stays out of the cycle, because it is the accent's hue, and gray is left for the key.
111|
112|Spacing stays the composer's: the gaps between ranks and zones, the zone margins and the board's margin. The router measures every clearance against that spacing, so a board that reads cramped is fixed in the model, as `references/style-guide.md` Section 7 sets out.
113|
114|---
115|
116|## 7. FLOORS
117|
118|A token that misses a floor falls back to its built-in value and the rest of the design stands. When the file changed two tokens that miss a floor together, one falls back at a time and the floors are measured again, so the other stands once the floor holds.
119|
120|| Floor | Measure |
121||---|---|
122|| Text on a fill | Each role's text colour on its fill at 4.5:1 or more |
123|| The accent's own pair | No role names the accent's pair |
124|| The accent's hue | 45 degrees or more from every saturated role stroke, zone tint, line colour and the key's tint on the board |
125|| The accent's contrast | Its stroke at 3:1 or more on white |
126|| The accent's weight | A node outline over 6 and up to 16 pixels, a message line heavier than the lines and up to 8 |
127|| Lines | 1 to 4 pixels, `line.color` at 3:1 or more on white and `line.async` and `line.lifeline` at 2:1 or more, because an open head also marks an async message and a lifeline is a guide |
128|| Dots | A start, an end, a merge and a fork carry no label, so the fill of the role each draws measures 3:1 or more on white |
129|| Kinds apart | No two kinds one type draws share a shape, a pair and an outline |
130|| Type | `small` 14 or more, `label` and `field` from `small` up to `node`, `node` 16 to 24, `zone` from `node` up to 24, the largest zone name the router keeps a zone's head clear for, `subtitle` from `zone` up to `title`, `title` from twice `node` up to 128 |
131|| Names | A role or the accent names a swatch, a kind names a role, the cycle and the key's tint name section tints, the cycle holds two or more tints once each and never the key's tint |
132|| Words | Key words and `meta.name` on one line of 40 characters or fewer, every character of them text |
133|
134|Three more rules keep a bad edit from passing silently:
135|
136|- A group or a token the composer does not read is left out, and a value of the wrong type falls back
137|- An edit to a swatch or a tint is ignored, because those are FigJam's own colours
138|- A file with no json block, two blocks, a block that does not parse or another `schemaVersion` falls back whole to the built-in design, and so does one the reader cannot handle for any other reason, so an edit never stops a board
139|
140|Do pick a role's swatch for what it means on every board, and keep the accent the only pink. Do not give two kinds of one type the same swatch and shape, and do not reach for a colour outside FigJam's pairs, because a custom colour drops out of FigJam's picker.
141|

# use_figma — Figma Plugin API Skill
Use the `use_figma` tool to execute JavaScript in Figma files via the Plugin API. All detailed reference docs live in `references/`.

When available, call `create_session` with `fileKey` and `description` before file reads or edits (create the file first if needed), then pass the returned `sessionId` unchanged to every call that accepts it, including follow-ups and work across files.

**Always include `figma-use` in the comma-separated `skillNames` parameter when calling `use_figma`. If this skill was loaded via an MCP resource, you MUST prefix the name with `resource:` (e.g. `resource:figma-use`).** This is a logging parameter used to track skill usage — it does not affect execution.

**If Figma MCP tools appear as deferred tools, batch-load all their schemas in a single `ToolSearch` call** using the `select:` syntax — e.g. `ToolSearch query="select:use_figma,get_screenshot,get_metadata,create_new_file"`. One round trip beats six.

**MANDATORY for visible design changes:** Before the first mutating `use_figma` call, load [figma-generate-design](../figma-generate-design/SKILL.md) alongside this skill and include both names in every mutating call’s `skillNames`. This applies from a single visible property or element to a full page, screen, or composed multi-section view—even when the user calls that view a component. `figma-use` provides the Plugin API rules; `figma-generate-design` provides design-system discovery through `search_design_system`, asset importing, and incremental assembly.

**Reusable library exception:** If the primary deliverable is a reusable component, component set, variant system, variable/token collection, style foundation, or other library asset intended for reuse or publication, load [figma-generate-library](../figma-generate-library/SKILL.md) instead. It provides the component-creation workflow—variable foundations, variant sets, and design-token bindings—that `figma-use` alone does not cover. For tasks that include both library assets and a composed design that uses them, load both companion skills. Read-only `use_figma` calls need neither.

Before anything, load [plugin-api-standalone.index.md](references/plugin-api-standalone.index.md) to understand what is possible. When you are asked to write plugin API code, use this context to grep [plugin-api-standalone.d.ts](references/plugin-api-standalone.d.ts) for relevant types, methods, and properties. This is the definitive source of truth for the API surface. It is a large typings file, so do not load it all at once, grep for relevant sections as needed.

IMPORTANT: Whenever you work with design systems, start with [working-with-design-systems/wwds.md](references/working-with-design-systems/wwds.md) to understand the key concepts, processes, and guidelines for working with design systems in Figma. Then load the more specific references for components, variables, text styles, and effect styles as needed.

## 1. Critical Rules
1.  **Use `return` to send data back.** The return value is JSON-serialized automatically (objects, arrays, strings, numbers). Do NOT call `figma.closePlugin()` or wrap code in an async IIFE — this is handled for you.
2.  **Write plain JavaScript with top-level `await` and `return`.** Code is automatically wrapped in an async context. Do NOT wrap in `(async () => { ... })()`.
3.  `figma.notify()` **throws "not implemented"** — never use it
3a. **Return node IDs and keep workflow state outside the Figma file.** Set human-readable component purpose and usage in `node.description` only on a `COMPONENT` or `COMPONENT_SET` — never on a frame or instance.
3b. **Narrow before accessing type-specific properties.** Check `node.type`, use a capability guard such as `"characters" in node`, or prefilter with `findAllWithCriteria`. `characters` requires a text-capable node; optional chaining does not protect unsupported property access.
4.  `console.log()` is NOT returned — use `return` for output
5.  **Size construction calls for safe retry and validate from evidence.** Do not split a working operation solely to create validation checkpoints. Batch related work when the resulting script remains safe to retry; a complete section or page may be built in one call. Split when crossing page context, when partial execution would be difficult to recover, or after an actual failure requires a targeted retry. Return affected IDs and relevant counts, names, or bounds from each write—this counts as structural validation. Run a separate structural check only when required evidence is missing or after a relevant mutation. Normally take one screenshot after composition and one after a visual fix. The most recent passing screenshot is the final check; do not repeat it when nothing relevant changed. Stop once requirements pass.
6.  Colors are **0–1 range** (not 0–255): `{r: 1, g: 0, b: 0}` = red. Paint `color` objects use `{r, g, b}` **only — no `a` field**; opacity goes at the paint level (`{ type: 'SOLID', color: {...}, opacity: 0.5 }`).
7.  Fills/strokes are **read-only arrays** — clone, modify, reassign
8.  **Every text edit follows the canonical recipe: load font → `await` → mutate → return affected node IDs.** Skipping the load throws `Cannot write to node with unloaded font "<family> <style>"`. The rule covers more than `characters` — it applies to any operation on nodes with unloaded fonts (`appendChild`, `insertChild`, `setBoundVariable`, `setExplicitVariableModeForCollection`, `setValueForMode`, `findAll` callbacks touching text). When mutating existing text, load the node's *current* fonts via `getStyledTextSegments(['fontName'])`, not a hardcoded default. Inter is preloaded in most environments so other families surface this bug more often — the recipe is the same for every font. Use `await figma.listAvailableFontsAsync()` first if the style string is unverified — **never guess** (`"SemiBold"` vs `"Semi Bold"` is a common footgun). For `FONT_FAMILY`-scoped variables, load every value across every relevant mode before `setBoundVariable("fontFamily", …)`, `setValueForMode`, or `setExplicitVariableModeForCollection`. `lineHeight`/`letterSpacing` take `{unit, value}`, not bare numbers. See [Canonical text-edit recipe](references/gotchas.md#canonical-text-edit-recipe-font-load--await--mutate--return-ids).
9.  **Pages load incrementally** — use `await figma.setCurrentPageAsync(page)` to switch pages and load their content. The sync setter `figma.currentPage = page` does **NOT** work and throws `"Setting figma.currentPage is not supported"`. Page context resets to the **first page** at the start of every `use_figma` call, so re-switch each call; switch **at most once per call** and fan multi-page work out in parallel — see [Page Rules](#2-page-rules-critical) and [gotchas.md](references/gotchas.md#set-current-page-once-per-use_figma-call--split-multi-page-work-into-parallel-calls).
10. `setBoundVariableForPaint` returns a **NEW** paint — must capture and reassign
11. `createVariable` accepts collection **object or ID string** (object preferred)
12. **`layoutSizingHorizontal/Vertical` is value-restricted by structural context — `FIXED` always works, `HUG` and `FILL` do not.** `'HUG'` is valid only on an auto-layout frame itself OR on a **TEXT** child of one. `'FILL'` is valid only on a child of an auto-layout frame that is also not absolute-positioned, not inside an immutable frame, and not a canvas-grid child.
